title: FM27 Skins — Install Paths, Platform Checks & Patch Recovery
description: FM27 skins for the released build: Priisek Retro 27 v1.5 and the Super League Turkey club skins. Two different install methods, exact Windows and macOS paths, and how to get your interface back after a patch.
meta: Updated 13 November 2026 · FM27 released 10 November 2026 · Author installation notes checked 13 November; neither skin has been tested in-game by this site.
body:
Two FM27 skin channels are active, and they install in different ways. Priisek Retro 27 ships a download with an installer; the Super League Turkey club skins are folders you drop into your own skins directory and then pick from the in-game settings. Getting the method wrong is the usual reason a skin “doesn't work”, so check which one you downloaded before you touch a file.

Which skin, and how it installs

SkinLatest release read 13 NovemberInstall methodKnown limits stated by the author
Priisek Retro 27 · Priisekv1.5, file dated 13 November; an installer was added on 11 NovemberRun the packaged installer, or use the Steam archive if you want to place the files yourselfAuthor answers Mac questions with “if you have the same folders and end point it should do”, which is a maybe rather than a confirmation; the changelog is still fixing background and white-on-white issues
Super League Turkey club skins · Emr1907Club packs dated 7 November (Galatasaray, Beşiktaş, Trabzonspor), earlier Fenerbahçe packs 29–30 OctoberCopy the club folder into your FM27 skins folder, then choose it under Preferences → Quick settings“The package has passed structural validation. It has not been claimed as in-game tested.” The page still says to close Football Manager 26 in one place — read FM27 for every path

The two install methods, copy-paste

Club skins (Super League Turkey, and the method to try first because it is reversible):

  1. Close FM27. Create the folder if it does not exist: Windows: Documents\Sports Interactive\Football Manager 27\skins macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Sports Interactive/Football Manager 27/skins
  2. Extract the club archive and copy the whole club folder — the one containing skin.json, main.uss, custom.uss, styles/, assets/, fonts/ — directly inside skins. No extra wrapper folder.
  3. Start FM27, open Preferences → Quick settings, select the club skin, accept the reload prompt.
  4. Check the main menu, tactics, squad and player screens, then a match day. If a screen breaks, select the previous skin in the same menu — no game files were changed, so that is the whole rollback.

Bundle-replacement skins (the older Turkey package, and how interface mods worked before FM27's settings menu):

  1. Close FM27 and Steam. Back up the three bundle files you are about to replace.
  2. Find the game's own StreamingAssets folder, not your Documents folder: Windows: Football Manager 27\fm_Data\StreamingAssets\aa\StandaloneWindows64\ macOS: Football Manager 27/fm.app/Contents/Resources/Data/StreamingAssets/aa/StandaloneOSX/
  3. Replace ui-mainmenu-assets_assets_all.bundle, ui-styles_assets_default.bundle and ui-tactics_assets_all.bundle with the package's versions, keeping the original filenames.
  4. Keep the originals in a folder you can find. A patch that touches the interface can leave the modified bundles incompatible, and restoring the originals is the only clean rollback.
The two methods are not interchangeable. A skins-folder package does nothing if you paste it into StreamingAssets, and a bundle package does not appear under Preferences → Quick settings.

Does it work on the 10 November build?

Partly confirmed, and the confirmation is indirect. Both authors published after launch — Priisek's installer and v1.5 changelog land on 11–13 November, the Turkey club packs on 7 November — so the files are being written against the released game. Neither page names a build number, and the Turkey author explicitly has not claimed an in-game test.

What the current changelogs are still fixing tells you where the risk sits: backgrounds, dark pitch rendering, and white-on-white text contrast. Those are exactly the screens worth checking first after you install.

Skins and logo/face packs are separate jobs

A logo pack's compatibility statement says nothing about interface assets. Logos and faces go into the graphics folder and survive a skin change; a skin replaces interface bundles or adds a skin definition and does not. Use the logo-pack page for badges and the mods page for names and faces.
